newsitem.title: UK: Willis profits hit by pound, competition.
newsitem.headline: Willis profits hit by pound, competition.

text.p: British insurance broker Willis Corroon Group Plc on Tuesday blamed the pound's strength and continuing competition for a sharp fall in profits for the first six months of the year.
Pre-tax profits slipped to 60.2 million pounds, broadly in line with analyst forecasts and down from 68.2 million pounds in the same period last year.
Brokerage and fee revenues from continuing operations for the first half fell to 335.6 million pounds from 364.2 million pounds.

Chairman John Reeve said the results were in line with expectations at the start of the year, which anticipated both the continuing acute pressures in its operating environment, particularly affecting the North American and some global specialty businesses, and the unhelpful effects of the strong pound.
These had an adverse impact of 6.6 million pounds, said Reeve.
The changing balance of the business had progressively reduced the proportion of annual profits in the earlier months of the year, a trend that was expected to continue, he added.
The results include 4.5 million pounds profit commission from the group's Lloyd's members' agency in respect of the 1994 underwriting year.
The decision to place subsidiary Sovereign Marine & General Insurance in liquidation had a neutral impact on profits but reduced earnings because deferred tax was considered no longer recoverable.

Reeve said the group had recently undertaken a number of initiatives to further the development of the business while continuing to implement the change programme instituted to realise the strategy introduced last year.
That included the acquisition of a stake in French broker Gras Savoye and raising its holding in Brazilian broker York Willis Corroon Corretores de Seguros to 100 percent.
Those moves reflected the aim of attaining leadership positions in chosen market sectors, said Reeve.
Willis also announced today the establishment of a joint IFA (independent financial advisory) business with Abbey National.
